answer: Because the counters live in the tundra ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. An operator running many aliases hence pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the dune quota and the river admission check. Submission rate is limited to 2 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole fleet from one uplink. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
